image_description: A museum display featuring a large Triceratops skull fossil mounted on a stand. The skull exhibits the characteristic three horns (two brow, one nasal) and a large solid frill. To the right, a partial vertebral column is visible. In the background, there is a glass case with a blue-lit diorama or model of a dinosaur, and a person is partially visible behind the glass. A label with text 'JBB50' is attached to the left side of the skull mount.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fossil clearly displays two large brow horns curving upward and a distinct, shorter nasal horn on the snout, matching the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As this is a fossilized skull, the keratinous beak (soft tissue) is not preserved. Only the bony rostral bone is visible, so the 'keratinous cutting edge' cannot be visually verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the skull and a portion of the spine; the body and limbs are not present in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, solid bony frill is clearly visible extending behind the skull, consistent with Triceratops morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) and shows texture consistent with fossilized bone, including marginal irregularities that correspond to epoccipitals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a bare fossil skull; no skin impressions or soft tissue are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the image.
The tail is not visible in the image.
